answer: Two witnesses sign the watchman's log at every halt, and the mirages he recorded are read against the march the caravan actually made. A ridge log written in one sitting fails the witnesses: at the pigment of the march the mirages must match the heat the caravan felt, and a sitting log invents water that never shimmered. Faking the log means hiring a watchman for three months, bribing two witnesses and paying 8,100, while the ember signature on each page is dated daily, so a log whose pages share one day's ink is burned.
